source_text: Qua culpa tu illas clades, quas supra enumeravimus, dicis accidisse naturae, ex quibus nec unam in his, qui ad Christi perveniunt sacramenta, constat sanari, ac per hoc multo plus iniquitatem primi hominis ad nocendum asseris habuisse virtutis, quam gratia Christi obtinet ad medendum, quo collecto ostensum est, quantam inter Catholicos et Manichaeos, tantam inter te et apostolum Paulum esse discordiam.
pass_a_gloss: By which fault you say those disasters, which we enumerated above, happened to nature, from which not even one is established to be healed in those who arrive at the sacraments of Christ, and through this you assert that the iniquity of the first human being had much more of virtue toward harming than the grace of Christ obtains toward healing, which having been collected it has been shown that as great a discord as between catholics and Manichaeans, so great is between you and the apostle Paul.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: You say that this fault brought upon nature the disasters listed above. Not even one of them, however, is known to be healed in those who come to Christ’s sacraments. Consequently, you assert that the first man’s wickedness had far more power to harm than Christ’s grace possesses to heal. This conclusion shows that the disagreement between you and the apostle Paul is as great as that between catholics and Manichaeans.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Scripture's destruction of iniquitas is the Law's purpose; keep moral injustice.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
